name: Halfshafts
description: Left/right IRS halfshafts with plunging inner and fixed outer CV joints, boots, clamps, inner circlips and axle nuts connecting the cradle-mounted differential to the rear hubs.

components.name: Rear halfshaft assembly (L/R)
components.description: Independent-rear-suspension drive shafts from the differential side gears to the rear hubs, each with a plunging inner CV and fixed outer CV. Left and right are different lengths/part numbers. On a race car with slicks and a race LSD, factory shafts are a known weak link under hard launches and curb strikes - upgraded shafts are common for high-power builds.
components.location: From diff outputs (x≈2.80, y≈0.36, z≈±0.17) to rear hub/knuckle (x≈2.811, y≈0.37, z≈±0.72). Left (+z) shown; mirrored.

factory.name: GM rear wheel drive shafts (L & R)
factory.notes: GM 84855967 is listed as the rear passenger-side half-shaft for Camaro (verify Gen 6 trim/VIN fitment). Sides are not interchangeable.

raceOptions.name: Upgraded IRS halfshafts for 2016+ Camaro
raceOptions.notes: DSS offers upgraded Camaro axle levels (rated by hp); confirm Gen 6 / eLSD spline application.

raceOptions.name: Custom race halfshafts with race CVs
raceOptions.notes: Pair with race LSD output splines when converting the diff.

fluids.name: CV joint grease
fluids.spec: Grease supplied with boot kit / joint (molybdenum CV grease); do not mix types
fluids.capacity: Per boot kit sachet (typically 80-120 g per joint)

installNotes: Install a seal protector on the diff side seal; slide inner stub in straight and tap with a soft mallet until the circlip snaps home - pull test by hand.
Feed outer stub through hub bearing; install new axle nut and washer, finger tight.
With wheels on ground (or brakes applied), torque axle nut to GM SI value.
Check CV angles at ride height - lowered race cars run larger angles; ensure boots are not stretched at full droop.
inspection: Circlip engagement after any diff work

components.name: CV boots (inner & outer)
components.description: Thermoplastic/rubber boots that keep grease in and grit out of each CV. The #1 halfshaft failure cause on track is a torn boot near the exhaust/diff cooler heat; heat-shield the inner boots if the exhaust runs close.
components.location: Over each inner and outer CV joint, both sides.

fluids.name: CV joint grease
fluids.spec: Grease supplied with boot kit / joint (molybdenum CV grease); do not mix types
fluids.capacity: Per boot kit sachet (typically 80-120 g per joint)

installNotes: Burp air from boot before final clamp so it is not ballooned/collapsed.
inspection: Splits, grease fling on wheel/brake area every event

components.name: Axle (hub) nut & washer
components.description: Retains the outer CV stub in the hub bearing and preloads the joint/bearing interface. Single-use on GM applications; under-torque leads to fretted splines and clicking.
components.location: Center of each rear hub, outboard (z≈±0.74).

factory.name: GM rear wheel drive shaft nut

hardware.tool: Large axle-nut socket, torque wrench ≥300 N·m
hardware.notes: Gen 6 GM SI may specify a torque+angle procedure - look it up before final torque. Torque with wheel on ground or brakes locked, never with an impact gun. Checked 2026-10: the TightTorque table compiled from the 2016-2018 Camaro service manual lists 'Rear wheel drive shaft nut 270 N·m (199 lb ft)', a Gen 6 value. The same table lists the rear wheel drive shaft to drive flange bolts (halfshaft to diff) at 50 N·m first pass; their final step is in SI.

installNotes: Torque after wheel bearing and knuckle are fully installed; recheck after shakedown.

sources.title: Camaro5 forum - rear axle nut torque discussion (5th-gen, 199 ft-lb cited, unverified)
